answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a velvet as the anchor of the cost.
